Auto-summary (auto):
- Goal: scope a 4-week POC to validate unit economics and perf for Codex Systems' customer-facing assistant.
- Key success criteria: P95 latency < 250ms for 512-token inference, cost per active user < $0.10/month projected at scale, stable QoS under burst to 50 QPS.
- Next: run benchmark (1k requests) with 2k token contexts, exchange cost model spreadsheet, share SOC2/KMS docs.

Topics: POC success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, per-token cost modeling, batching & caching knobs, budget constraints, timeline and ops integration.

00:00:00 - Lena: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um quick intros on our side, I'm Lena Park AE at Redwood, Omar and Priya from SEs are here.
00:00:12 - Marcus: Marcus Lee here, Head of ML at Codex, Sara on platform and David is on for CTO oversight.
00:00:25 - Lena: cool, goal for today is to scope the POC - success criteria, what we need to run benchmarks and importantly cost modeling, ok?
00:00:40 - Omar: quick q, Marcus, can you describe current traffic shapes? QPS, prompt sizes, typical peaks?
00:00:52 - Marcus: yeah so avg QPS is about 5 steady, peaks hit 45-50 for 10-15 minute windows; average prompt about 120 tokens, avg completion 60 tokens but there are long tails - long contexts up to 2k tokens for some enterprise users.
00:01:17 - Sara: we have a 99th percentile latency target for user interactions of 300ms, but we'd like to hit 200ms P95 if possible.
00:01:30 - Omar: ok that maps well to Redwood; two knobs to consider for cost: batching size (improves GPU utilization) and prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts. Also quantization options affect perf/cost.
00:01:46 - Marcus: can you give a ballpark per-token estimate? we need to justify budgets to finance.
00:01:55 - Priya: rough quick answer: hosted infra per-token cost depends on model & quantization; for a 13B open model on rtx-class hardware at good batching we typically see something like 0.0004-0.0010 USD per input+output token range; but this is super dependent on batch policy, cache hit rate, and average seq length.
00:02:20 - Marcus: ok so at avg prompt 120 + 60 = 180 tokens, that's about $0.072-0.18 per request? that seems high.
00:02:33 - Lena: yes so important to note output tokens cost too, and we often amortize by batching across concurrent requests; also prefix caching can cut cost dramatically for repeated system prompts or session state. If you have high cache hit rates (like 40-70%), unit cost drops a lot.
00:02:55 - David: can you walk through a simple model: given 5 steady QPS and a projected 10k DAUs, what does monthly look like?
00:03:06 - Omar: sure quick calc on call - if avg tokens per interaction 180, 5 QPS steady equals ~432k tokens/hour or 10.4M tokens/day, monthly ~312M tokens. At $0.0006/token that's about $187k/month - but batching and caching could reduce effective token-scan cost by 2-4x depending on hit rates.
00:03:40 - Sara: those numbers need to be compared to our current vendor spend; we pay about $120k/month today for lower-quality model access so the delta matters.
00:03:52 - Priya: additional lever is model size/architecture: switching to a 7B tuned variant may reduce compute cost by ~40-60% while preserving quality for your tasks; Redwood's model catalog can test variants.
00:04:10 - Marcus: timeline - we're targeting a 4 week POC to validate perf and cost assumptions before committing to a dedicated contract. Does that timeframe make sense?
00:04:20 - Lena: yep typical. Week 0: onboarding + sample data + instrumentation; Week 1-2: run benchmarks and iterate; Week 3: integrate with routing and caching knobs; Week 4: finalize cost model + exec summary.
00:04:35 - Lina: procurement question - if we go Dedicated later, what's the contract cadence? we prefer monthly to start.
00:04:44 - Lena: Redwood Dedicated supports monthly reserved capacity but enterprise pricing is flexible; we'll include options in the follow-up pricing sheet.
00:04:55 - 00:05:30 - [small cross talk about access and firewall rules, "VPC peering" misheard as "VPC pairing"]
00:05:31 - Omar: for the benchmark we need: 1) a representative prompt set (we'll take a 200-300 sample) 2) target concurrency matrix (steady, 2x, 10x bursts) 3) token length distribution - we saw you have a long tail to 2k. We'll simulate both 512 and 2k contexts.
00:06:05 - Marcus: we can provide logs and a small offline dataset. We'll also provide 2 weeks of production telemetry.
00:06:12 - Priya: great, we'll run two benchmark passes: one with hosted Redwood in our region, and one on Redwood Dedicated-compatible config (to estimate reserved cost). We'll capture latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and effective per-request cost.
00:06:30 - Marcus: how do you compute "effective per-request cost" again?
00:06:34 - Omar: we take the raw GPU runtime cost (instance hourly), amortize across tokens processed in the run, add networking and orchestration overhead, then apply observed cache hit rate and batching throughput to compute effective per-inference cost. We'll output per-token and per-session numbers.
00:06:54 - Marcus: ok, give me a worked example for our numbers to make it concrete.
00:06:58 - Omar: assume 1 x A10-equivalent GPU at $3/hour (example), you can process ~200 tokens/sec depending on model and batch; that's 720k tokens/hour, so raw compute cost per token ~0.0000042 - but these numbers vary; sorry that's maybe optimistic, typical realistic numbers for medium models land in mid-0.000x to 0.001 range after accounting for all layers. The easiest path is run the benchmark and we'll produce the spreadsheet with low/expected/high scenarios.
00:07:30 - Sara: what about batching increases latency; can you keep P95 targets with large batch sizes?
00:07:36 - Priya: there's a tradeoff: large batch sizes reduce per-token cost but increase tail latency; Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching which tries to honor latency SLOs by dynamically sizing batches and auto-fallback. For your 200ms P95 target on 512 token runs we can tune batch window to keep P95 <250ms while still getting cost improvements.
00:08:00 - Marcus: caching - we have repeated system prompts across many sessions, how much can caching help?
00:08:06 - Omar: prefix/KV-cache helps mainly when there's repeated context; for system prompts and short conversation histories, hit rates of 30-60% are common which can reduce token compute by same percent for cached prefixes. We also offer session-level caching and deduplication heuristics.
00:08:26 - Marcus: any common gotchas?
00:08:29 - Priya: watch out for context-window overhead when you switch to 2k tokens - memory increases and kernel selection changes which can cause nonlinear cost increases; quantization can help but may affect quality. Also network overhead if you choose hosted vs private egress.
00:08:49 - David: about security - we need SOC2, KMS integrations and to ensure logs are retained for audits. Can you share docs?
00:08:57 - Lena: yes we'll share SOC2, ISO and KMS integration docs and a template for VPC peering.
00:09:07 - Marcus: acceptance criteria - we propose: (1) P95 latency <= 250ms on 512-token workload, (2) effective cost per DAU < $0.10 projected at 10k DAUs after caching assumptions, (3) no regressions on quality compared to our current baseline.
00:09:25 - Lena: that's clear. We'll add that to the POC charter and align on measurement definitions (how you compute DAU, how many sessions).

00:11:38 - Marcus: can we include a run that uses the same temperature/decoding settings as prod? We use top_p 0.95 and temp 0.2.
00:11:46 - Priya: yes we'll match your decoding settings. Also we'll test a smaller 7B variant to quantify quality delta vs cost.
00:11:55 - Sara: how long do these runs take?
00:12:00 - Omar: the 1k request run should take ~10-20 minutes to execute plus analysis time; full matrix runs with bursts and 2k context could take a couple hours but we can parallelize.
